# Figure captions (generated by make_figures.py)

Fig. 1. Monthly share of unreliable decision forecasts (|f(w_t) − p̄_t| > AUD 300/MWh) across the five NEM regions. Shading marks the fit (72,865 intervals), validation (14,640), test (14,650) and 2023–25 replication (261,635) periods. October 2022 (hatched) is excluded because the AEMO archive holds only the latest pre-dispatch run for that month. The y-axis is cut at 5%; the June 2022 value (25.7%, marked ▲) falls in the administered-pricing period.

Fig. 3. Information timeline for one trading interval. Features use only pre-dispatch runs published up to the decision run (shaded). The label compares the decision forecast f(w_t) with the mean of the six settled 5-min DISPATCHPRICE values (INTERVENTION = 0): Y_t = 1[|f(w_t) − p̄_t| > δ_Y], δ_Y = AUD 300/MWh. Run spacing is schematic; the time axis is broken.

Fig. 4. Mean absolute error of the decision forecast against the settled price in extreme and normal intervals, 2023–25 (R1; log scale). Labels give the ratio of means (28–56); Welch p < 0.001 in every region.

Fig. 5. ROC (a) and precision–recall (b) curves of the FRI model, fitted on 2021–22 and frozen, on the 2022 test set (14,650 intervals, 94 unreliable) and the 2023–25 replication (261,635 intervals). The dash-dot curve is raw recent_std_3h on 2023–25 (R4 comparison). Dotted curves rank intervals by the decision forecast alone, |f(w_t)| (exploratory, not registered).

Fig. 6. Feature importance of the FRI model (17 features; mean |SHAP value| (TreeSHAP) on the 2022 test set, as % of the total). The decision forecast accounts for 44.2% and the revision-path group for 37.1%.

Fig. 7. Energy discharged into over-forecast intervals (f(w_t) − p̄_t > AUD 300/MWh) by agent, β = 2.03. FRI reduces exposure against the baseline by 68.5% in 2022 (95% CI [0.0, 100.8] MWh) and by 47.0% in 2023–25 (vol - FRI 557.6 MWh [387.7, 744.6]; R3). * Exploratory control, not registered: same band counts as FRI, assigned by highest f(w_t).

Fig. 8. Net-revenue advantage of constant ×0.25 dispatch over FRI as degradation becomes less convex (R6), as a percentage of FRI net revenue. α is rescaled at each β so that baseline degradation cost is unchanged. The advantage falls from +115% (2022) and +35% (2023–25) at β = 2.03 to -3% and -5% at β = 1.0. FRI and baseline net revenue differ by at most 1.0% at any β (Table VII).

Fig. 9. AUC by region for the frozen FRI model (exploratory). n+ is the number of unreliable intervals in 2023–25 and in the 2022 test. 2022 AUC is shown only for regions with at least 10 unreliable intervals. The dashed line is the pooled 2023–25 AUC (R2).
